newsitem.title: USA: U.S. foreign crudes step aside for futures rally.
newsitem.headline: U.S. foreign crudes step aside for futures rally.

text.p: Sharp gains on the NYMEX futures market pushed aside interest in the U.S. foreign crude sector on Monday, with talk for physical barrels quiet.
"There was nothing talked today about bringing foreign barrels to the Gulf," said one crude broker.
Late in the day, crude traders valued the trans-Atlantic arbitrage between February West Texas Intermediate and Brent at $1.20, steady from earlier in the session.
A pair of dated Brent deals were established early in the U.S. session, getting done in London time at January Brent minus 20 cents and January Brent minus 15 cents, both for December 27-29 dates.
The Brent deal at minus 20 cents represented a 20 cents decline from the previous trades seen on Thursday.
Paper Brent spreads were steady all session, getting done at plus 47 and 50 cents in London, then again for two separate deals in the U.S. aftermarket at plus 47 cents again.

Traders said they spotted only nominal interest in the U.S. window, with the only other paper moved a small parcel of February Brent at $23.75 a barrel, 10 cents weaker than the IPE settlement price of $23.85 a barrel.
"It was very active on the futures side of business, but quiet on the cash," said a trader.

NYMEX January spot futures rose drastically to settle $1.27 higher at $25.74 a barrel. Winter weather forecasts calling for extreme Arctic cold spells for vast swaths of the U.S. this week and next prompted most of the buying, traders said.
In other talk, North Sea Ekofisk and Forties cargoes were heard sold, but prices could not be confirmed.
The Ekofisk crude loading program released on Monday showed an increase of four cargoes over December. Ekofisk continued the trend calling for a small rise in total North Sea production in January.
